summary: Describes server-based sorting and threading extensions for IMAP. They let the server do the sorting and grouping into conversations, which can greatly improve performance for clients showing sorted or threaded views. It is a standards-track specification.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 5256 adds IMAP commands for sorting messages and grouping them into threads on the server. The server returns an ordered list or a nested thread structure for the client to display.

subtitle: How IMAP servers sort mailbox messages and group them into conversation threads.

tldr.problem: A mail client may need to download message data before it can sort a mailbox or group messages into conversations.
tldr.mechanism: The SORT and THREAD commands let an IMAP server search and organize messages, returning message numbers or nested thread lists. THREAD defines ORDEREDSUBJECT and REFERENCES algorithms.
tldr.outcome: Clients can request organized results without downloading all message data first. RFC 5256 is updated by RFC 5957.

facts.label: Sort keys
facts.value: ARRIVAL, CC, DATE, FROM, SIZE, SUBJECT, TO

today: RFC 5256 is a Proposed Standard published in June 2008 and is updated by RFC 5957.

sections.title: Server-Side Sorting and Threading
sections.content:
The SORT and THREAD extensions let an IMAP server organize messages without requiring the client to download the data and perform the work itself. Servers announce support using a SORT capability or a THREAD capability followed by an algorithm name.

Both extensions use the same base-subject extraction and collation rules so connected servers and disconnected clients can produce consistent results. The mandatory character sets are US-ASCII and UTF-8.
sections.plainLanguage: The client can ask the server to sort messages or group them into conversations. It receives the result without first downloading every message.

sections.title: Base Subjects and Sent Dates
sections.content:
Sorting and threading use a base subject, which removes common subject artifacts such as reply and forward prefixes, bracketed tags, and the “(fwd)” trailer. The RFC specifies a step-by-step procedure, and servers and disconnected clients MUST use the same procedure.

The sent date comes from the Date header adjusted to UTC. If it is missing or cannot be parsed, the message's INTERNALDATE is used. When dates match exactly, mailbox sequence order breaks the tie.
sections.plainLanguage: Before comparing subjects, the server removes common reply and forward markers. It adjusts message dates to a shared time zone and uses mailbox order to break exact ties.

sections.title: The SORT Command
sections.content:
SORT searches the mailbox and returns matching messages in the requested order. Its arguments include a list of sort keys, a required character set, and search criteria. The keys include ARRIVAL, CC, DATE, FROM, SIZE, SUBJECT, and TO. UID SORT returns unique identifiers instead of sequence numbers.

Sort order is ascending unless REVERSE applies to a criterion. With multiple criteria, earlier criteria take priority. If messages tie on all requested criteria, their mailbox sequence order is used as an implicit final criterion.
sections.plainLanguage: SORT returns matching message numbers in the order the client requests, such as by sender and then date. Mailbox order breaks ties that remain.

sections.title: The THREAD Command and Its Algorithms
sections.content:
THREAD returns matching messages grouped into conversations. ORDEREDSUBJECT groups messages by base subject and orders them by sent date. Its structure is shallow: the first message is the root, and later messages are children of that first message.

REFERENCES uses References and In-Reply-To headers to build parent-and-child relationships, then uses subjects to merge related threads. It creates temporary placeholders for referenced messages that are missing, removes those placeholders later, and avoids links that would create loops. Message IDs are normalized before comparison; subject comparisons are case-insensitive.
sections.plainLanguage: ORDEREDSUBJECT groups messages with the same cleaned subject. REFERENCES follows message-reply links to build a deeper conversation tree, then uses the subject to combine related branches.

sections.title: Reading SORT and THREAD Responses
sections.content:
A SORT response is a space-separated list of message sequence numbers, or unique identifiers for UID SORT. A THREAD response contains parenthesized thread lists. Numbers in sequence represent parent and child messages; nested lists show where a conversation branches.

The THREAD response can contain messages whose parent is not included in the search result or is absent from the mailbox. The protocol does not limit how deeply a thread may be nested.
sections.plainLanguage: SORT returns a list of message numbers. THREAD uses nested parentheses to show which messages reply to others and where a conversation splits.
